subject: Post-call: FineEdge performance SLOs + benchmark methodology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finedge.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finedge.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: FineEdge performance SLOs + benchmark methodology

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re aligned on scope for the performance qualification: 

Summary of what you shared:
- Latency targets: p95 <= 250ms for text-generation (up to 1024 tokens) for interactive UI flows.
- Throughput: sustained 300 requests/minute (5 rps) with bursts to 50 rps for short periods.
- Concurrency: expected concurrency of 60 concurrent users during peak hour.
- Streaming: UI requires token-by-token streaming for partial responses (client shows tokens as they arrive).

Redwood ask / clarifying items we need to validate:
1) Representative prompt set: if you can share 100–200 sample prompts (short, mid, long) we’ll use those for reproducible runs.
2) Definition of tokens/normalization: confirm whether you’re using OpenAI tokenization or a byte-pair tokenizer baseline; this affects measured latency for long sequences.
3) Warm-up vs measured window: do you want cold-start included in SLOs, or measure after a fixed warm-up (we usually report both).
4) Target hardware: we’ll run initial benchmarks on our dedicated A100 80GB config unless you prefer an alternate GPU.

Proposed next steps:
- Alex: share sample prompts and any mandatory blacklists / refusal cases (by EOD Friday).
- Priya: confirm whether p95 target includes streaming overhead (i.e., first-token latency) or full-response latency.
- We (Marissa + Dev): exchange benchmark methodology doc + harness and run an initial reproducible test by end of next week.

I attached a short rubric of typical measurements and will follow up with Dev (SE) for the methodology doc.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — solid recap. A couple clarifications: 

- For p95 we care about first meaningful token latency (client experience), though we’ll also want full-response timings for larger outputs. If first-token p95 <= 250ms we’re happy.
- Tokenization: we use the standard GPT-like tokenizer (BPE) for counting tokens; will include a note.
- Cold start: acceptable to exclude cold-start from SLO if documented (we care mostly about steady-state).

I’ve attached a seed sample of 120 prompts (mix of short chat, code, and long-form summarization); will share the final set in a CSV tomorrow. Priya and I can review the methodology once you send it.

Appreciate the quick turnaround on the harness.
Alex

Dev — looping you in to propose the benchmark harness & measurement definitions. Key constraints:
- Run on A100-80GB topology (single model-instance measurements then multi-instance to validate concurrency).
- Measure first-token p50/p95 and full-response p50/p95.
- Throughput sustained window = 5 minutes after warm-up.

Can you attach the methodology doc and a runnable harness (or link to the repo) we can run against the prompt CSV Alex will provide? Also include reproducibility notes: random seeds, model-version pinning, model compilation flags, and a clear hardware spec.

Hi all — attaching the initial benchmark methodology and prompt harness notes. Summary of methodology (high level):

1) Environment / hardware:
- GPU: NVIDIA A100 80GB (single-socket), CUDA 12.x, cuDNN verified.
- Node: 64 vCPU, 256GB RAM, NVMe local for model weights cache.
- Runtime: Redwood inference engine v2.4.1 (we’ll include exact git commit in the PDF).

2) Model & inputs:
- Model pinned to: open-llama-13b-v2-quant (or specify customer model if they supply one).
- Tokenization: GPT-style BPE. Prompts: use finedge_benchmark_prompts_v2.csv (120 prompts).

3) Measurement definitions:
- Warm-up: 120s of steady single-threaded traffic (no reporting).
- Measurement window: subsequent 5-minute window; report p50/p95/p99 for first-token and full-response.
- Throughput: measured as sustained requests/sec during window; QPS computed both aggregate and per-model-instance.
- Concurrency: ramp users to target concurrency over 2 minutes and hold for 3 minutes; measure tail latency.
- Streaming: capture TTFB (time to first byte/token) and token inter-arrival times. For streaming SLOs we’ll report first-token p95.
- Reproducibility: each experiment run = 3 independent runs with fixed seed (seed value logged). We’ll publish raw trace logs and harness commands.

4) Reporting artifacts:
- CSVs with per-request timings, raw event traces, and summarization scripts.
- A PDF methodology doc (attached) with exact commands, environment variables, and driver/kernel versions.

5) Caveats:
- If customer brings their own model, we’ll ensure quantization and compilation flags are matched.
- Network overheads: we’ll run initial tests on colocated host network; cross-region latency excluded unless requested.

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_methodology_v1.pdf, finedge_benchmark_prompts_v2.csv

Let me know if you want additional metrics (p99.9, jitter) or if you’d prefer wall-clock vs CPU-based timers.

– Dev

dev.patel@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: FineEdge performance SLOs + benchmark methodology

Adding two quick implementation notes from the runtime side:

- KV-prefix caching: for chat-style prompts we’ll exercise prefix caching in a separate run. Cache hit/miss breakdowns will be included; please confirm if FineEdge expects caching to be part of their SLO baseline.
- Batching policy: our harness will run both single-request path and an auto-batching path (batch sizes and latency tradeoffs reported). For interactive p95 targets we recommend conservative batching (max batch size 16) to avoid tail-latency spikes.

Also, for streaming measurements we’ll provide per-token latency percentiles (median inter-token and p95 inter-token). That helps debug UI jitter vs overall first-token latency.

If FineEdge wants to reproduce locally we can provide a dockerized harness + a runbook.

Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this looks great and very thorough. A couple quick confirmations: 

- FineEdge confirms we want prefix-caching included for chat sessions (50% of traffic will be multi-turn). Please include cache-hit normalized p95 numbers and a run showing no-cache baseline.
- For streaming SLO we’ll accept first-token p95 <= 250ms on steady-state with conservative batching (max batch 16).
- Please include the exact commit hash and compilation flags in the PDF so our infra team can reproduce.

Next steps: once we have the final prompt CSV and your harness, we’ll hand off to infra to run a mirrored test on our side (we’ll share results and any discrepancies). Can we aim to have Redwood’s initial run completed by Mar 6?

Thanks,
Priya
Director, Platform Engineering, FineEdge
